samples.title: Factorising is just un-multiplying
samples.subject: Maths
samples.script: You know how to multiply two brackets - factorising is walking that road backwards. Think of eighteen sweets: which two packets made them? Same idea here. Six x squared minus seven x minus three. I need two numbers that multiply to minus eighteen and add to minus seven. Try them like counting taxi change: minus nine and two. Split, group, and the brackets fall out on their own. No magic. If you can unpack a shopping bag, you can un-multiply an expression.
